---
title: "First-capture-conditional capture-recapture"
output: html_document
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(CJSModels)
```

`drm_cjs()` fits a fixed-effects Cormack–Jolly–Seber model conditional on each
animal's first capture. The survival formula models logit unit-time apparent
survival. Over an interval of length $\Delta$, survival is
$\phi_{\mathrm{unit}}^{\Delta}$; the
detection formula models detection conditional on being alive and surveyed.
This route does not estimate abundance or unseen animals.

Apparent survival combines mortality and permanent emigration; this model
cannot separate them. The contract also excludes all-zero histories, unknown
entry, recruitment, tag loss, temporary emigration, and behavioural trap
dependence. A history whose first capture is its final observation contributes
likelihood one because it has no post-capture information.

## Fit a model

```{r fit}
y <- rbind(
  c(1, 0, 0, 0), c(1, 0, 1, 0), c(1, 1, 0, 0), c(1, 1, 1, 0),
  c(1, 0, 0, 1), c(1, 0, 1, 1), c(1, 1, 0, 1), c(1, 1, 1, 1)
)
d <- cmr_data(y, id = seq_len(nrow(y)), occasions = 1:4, units = "years",
              frequency = c(12, 4, 8, 4, 4, 4, 4, 4))
fit <- drm_cjs(d, phi = ~1, p = ~1)
coef(fit)
```

## Predict and simulate conditionally

Training predictions return only keyed interval and occasion rows that
contribute to the objective.

```{r predict}
pred <- predict(fit)
head(pred$phi[c("id", "interval_start", "phi_unit", "phi_interval")])
head(pred$p)
```

Simulation retains the observed first-capture times, survey masks, and
administrative endpoints. It conditions on the first-capture emission and
keeps death absorbing. Supplying a seed gives reproducible data without
changing the caller's random-number stream.

```{r simulate}
simulated <- simulate(
  fit, nsim = 1L, seed = 20261006
)[[1L]]
refit <- drm_cjs(
  simulated$data, phi = ~1, p = ~1,
  phi_data = simulated$phi_data, p_data = simulated$p_data
)
coef(refit)
```

## Inspect fixed-effect intervals

Wald and profile intervals use the CJS-specific observed likelihood curvature
and constrained CJS refits, respectively. The parametric bootstrap retains
every attempt and its status when the original fit passes admission; an
ineligible original fit can be rejected before an interval result is returned.
Returned results expose a status for each coefficient.
These methods have not passed repeated-sample interval-availability or coverage
qualification. The current checks report only target-specific single-fit endpoint
capability and status; repeated-sample availability and calibration remain open. An available interval does not establish nominal calibration.

```{r intervals}
ci <- confint(fit, method = "wald")
attr(ci, "target_status")
```



## Scope

This example covers fixed effects only. Shared, individual, SD and selection routes remain experimental; extraction-specific combinations and scientific recovery/coverage checks are not established by this article.
